title: Frontend Architecture - Component Library
summary: Decided to build internal component library instead of adopting third-party solution. Established design tokens, accessibility standards, and documentation requirements.
decisions: Build internal component library - avoid third-party dependencies
WCAG 2.1 AA compliance mandatory for all components
Storybook for documentation and visual testing
Design tokens managed in Figma, synced to code
Target: 30 core components by end of Q2
transcription: [16:00] Rachel Zhao: Frontend architecture discussion. Main topic: component library strategy. [16:03] Tom Bradley: We've outgrown our current approach. Too much inconsistency across teams. [16:07] Rachel Zhao: Options are: adopt Material-UI or similar, or build our own. [16:10] Alex Rivera: MUI is bloated. We only use 30% of it. Bundle size is hurting performance. [16:15] Emma Liu: And styling overrides are painful. Every customization fights the framework. [16:19] Jen Park: From product side, we need more flexibility than off-the-shelf solutions provide. [16:22] Rachel Zhao: Sounds like consensus for building our own. Scope? [16:25] Tom Bradley: Start with 15 core components. Button, input, modal, table, etc. [16:30] Rachel Zhao: Accessibility requirements? [16:32] Emma Liu: WCAG 2.1 AA minimum. We have users with disabilities, it's non-negotiable.

actions.text: Set up component library repo and CI/CD

risks.description: Internal library may lack features teams need
